Analogical Reasoning Instructions:

The highest-transfer analogue (0.8157) shows only 24% brain penetration relative to plasma in rat, making it the strongest individual anchor because it combines the highest transfer score with a direct systemic brain-penetration measurement. Its structure contains an ionizable piperidine and several polar functionalities but is not an obvious extreme BBB non-penetrant. The next three analogues have closely matched transfer scores (0.7874, 0.7855, and 0.7800) and independently support the same direction. The pattern continues at 0.7708 and 0.7603, where biodistribution and brain-to-blood measurements again show poor CNS exposure.
